thread:
Olivia: Filing follow-up from Cust-Lyra Dedicated postmortem. Bottom line: intermittent VPC peer blackholes during a control-plane rolling deploy + on-prem NAT translation exhaustion caused partial node isolation. Summarized actions below.

Raj: Need owners + tight ETAs. Is this a sporadic bug or a repeating pattern across Dedicated installs?

Mei: This lines up with a repeating pattern we've flagged: control-plane churn -> peering route flap -> burst of short-lived TCP flows -> conntrack/NAT exhaustion on customer gateway. We've observed variations at 4 customers in the last 9 months.

Carlos: Lab repro notes: forced a route withdrawal while running synthetic short-lived TCP clients; observed missed SYNs and conntrack overflows. Kernel excerpt: ```
May 02 09:40:11 gw kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
May 02 09:40:11 gw custom-fw: NAT translation pool exhausted
```

Raj: Proposed owners:
- Mei: peering stability, routing fallback policy, and per-tenant telemetry (owner, ETA 7d)
- Carlos: on-prem reproducibility artifacts, NAT sizing guidance, and runbook updates (owner, ETA 5d)
- Olivia: customer comms, SLA impact, and exec notes (owner, ETA 4h for initial notice)
- Raj: program-level remediation & cross-customer correlation (owner, ETA 14d)

Olivia: Short-term mitigations to apply immediately:
- enable tenant-level fallback to regional replica for Cust-Lyra (rollback-ready) 120m ETA
- push keepalive and tcp_tw_reuse tuning on edge node (tcp_keepalive_time=15, tcp_tw_reuse=1) 30m ETA
- send customers a brief status update (Olivia) 30m ETA

Carlos: Mid/long actions:
- add conntrack utilization alert and automated remediation play (scale NAT pool or trigger fallback) (ETA 5d)
- publish "Dedicated on-prem NAT sizing" doc with formulas and examples (ETA 7d)
- implement per-tenant conntrack tracking and retention in peering telemetry (ETA 21d)

Mei: Network actions:
- small immediate: add short BFD/keepalive tweaks for peering control-plane so we detect flaps faster (ETA 48h)
- mid: circuit-breaker to reduce client churn impact during peering instability (policy: gradual drain + sticky fallback) (ETA 14d)
- long: quarterly peering stress test matrix across cloud regions and customer sandpits (ETA 60d)

DeployBot: Tickets created: INC-60001, REM-60002, CS-60003. Links: https://jira.redwood/INC-60001, https://jira.redwood/REM-60002

Olivia: Draft to customer: "We've applied temporary routing fallbacks and are monitoring your cluster closely. We're working on a permanent remediation plan and will share a detailed timeline within 10 business days." Approve?

Carlos: Approve. Adding runbook note to explicitly check conntrack headroom before any Dedicated cutover.

Raj: Cross-customer follow-up: correlate peering BGP flap events with our control-plane deploy windows for the past 365 days to surface high-risk deploy windows. Owner: Raj. ETA: 2025-08-01. Add results to REM-60002.

Mei: Quick repro snippet for the runbook (non-destructive lab): ```
# lightweight synthetic churn against peer while toggling route
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do hping3 -S -p 443 -c 200 --fast $PEER_IP & sleep 1; ip route del $PEER_PREFIX; sleep 2; ip route add $PEER_PREFIX via $GW; sleep 5; done; dmesg | tail -n 40 | grep -i conntrack
```

Olivia: Good. Please attach lab logs and kernel dumps to REM-60002 and update Jira owners. We'll add this to the monthly "peering review" slot and track recurring patterns there. If anyone hits blockers escalate to #eng-oncall. Closing after cadence notes are posted. :thumbsup:

Carlos: Uploading logs to REM-60002 now. Also adding a short checklist to the CS runbook: "Validate NAT pool sizing and conntrack headroom before Dedicated cutover."

Raj: I'll draft a short proposal for a deploy-damping window for active peering customers to reduce simultaneous control-plane churn exposure. Posting in eng-platform later today.

Mei: ack. Will start instrumenting per-tenant retransmit counters in peering telemetry and post progress in REM-60002.
